text.p: Pharmaceutical group F.H. Faulding and Co Ltd said on Wednesday it was looking at improved profit growth for 1996/97 and more substantial rises in profitability in the following two years.

Faulding chief executive officer Ed Tweddell told Reuters this financial year's result depended on the success of new products in the United States, meeting modest budget expectations in China, and improving the consumer health business in Australia. "If we get all those together, we are looking forward to nice profit growth (in 1996/97)," he said.

"This year I think is going to be a very interesting year for our group, but it is the next couple of years where we should see a substantial - given all the breaks, the vagaries of the world, the (US Food and Drug Administration) etc - increase in profitability," he said.

"(This would be) driven by the turnaround in the United States to go from loss to profit....but also growth everywhere else with the possible exception of China which I admit we are finding tough," he said.
